free_tier.stated: No data-volume limit. A 2025 peer-reviewed comparison of Zenodo and ScienceDB in Journal of Agricultural Big Data states it plainly: for ScienceDB the 数据大小 row reads '没有数据量的限制，用户可以上传任意大小的数据集' (no limit on data volume; users may upload datasets of any size), against Zenodo's 'max 50 GB, can be raised to 200 GB in one step'. Datasets above 2,000 files or above 1 TB are merely flagged 'restricted' pending an email. A negotiable ceiling, not a hard one.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Free, anonymous for public datasets. DOI resolution works (302 to the dataset page).

tooling: Explicitly two upload paths: '浏览器在线上传和FTP客户端在线上传'. Browser and FTP client. FTP is the one that matters at TB scale and is unusual among research repositories. There is also an Open API and OAI-PMH listed in the help centre. Login accepts a native account or third-party GitHub / ORCID / CAS / WeChat. And the English help page lists GitHub explicitly, which is the route that avoids Chinese identity requirements entirely.
chaining: Unlimited datasets per account with no per-user aggregate cap, so capacity is datasets × a negotiable per-dataset ceiling. FTP ingest means an unattended rclone or lftp job.

limits_note: Write-gated by 'formal review' (形式审核) of upload completeness, accessibility and the data-availability statement. Light-touch but still a human queue. Every dataset must have a subject category from the PRC GB/T 13745-2009 classification and at least three keywords. Metadata is mandatory and detailed (data generation procedure, temporal/spatial scope, per-file description). Some submission flows route through a CAS email or CSD account, which for the foreign client means using the GitHub/ORCID button rather than the native form.
reliability_note: Public JSON endpoints differ from Zenodo conventions. Specific API download paths returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-21 while dataset web pages resolved normally. Following DOI redirects (`/detail?dataSetId=...`) provides the standard path to download assets.

extras.agent_focus: 2026-era research-data and data-marketplace platforms, deliberately judged on the BINDING constraint (does a person with only an email get past the write gate?) rather than on the marketing quota. Coverage: IEEE DataPort (the wave-7 discovery this slot confirms and extends), Mozilla Data Collective (2025 launch, the only new ≥100 GB-per-file free host found), Source Cooperative re-probed at the byte level, the French national Dataverse (Recherche Data Gouv) as the one genuinely EU-funded space with a self-serve email account, plus the 2026 data-marketplace entrants (Snowflake, Databricks Free Edition, data.world, Datarade, Tableland, Spice.ai, DataChain), the EU Data Spaces (Gaia-X / Catena-X / EOSC EU Node / DICE) and ResearchGate/Academia.edu data upload. Two structural results dominate: (a) the 'data marketplace' category is uniformly not storage — they are catalogues, and every one of them fails on per-object size by two to three orders of magnitude; (b) the EU Data Spaces are real and large but gated on eduGAIN/eIDAS identity, so they are closed on identity exactly like CSC Allas and LUMI-O before them.

binding_note: the write is a queue with a person or a rule in it, so the upload rate is set by somebody else
